name: Meridian Munitions Precision Carbine MPC-9 'Scalpel'
description:
The MPC-9 Scalpel is a compact designated marksman rifle designed for urban precision work where a full-length DMR is too cumbersome. The weapon chambers 6.5mm caseless through a 400mm barrel — short for a precision platform — but compensates with a BCI-integrated ballistic computer that wrings maximum accuracy from the abbreviated barrel length. The result is a weapon that delivers 1-MOA accuracy at 600 meters in a package not much larger than a carbine.

Meridian's open-architecture philosophy extends to the Scalpel's optics rail, which accepts any manufacturer's scope or smart-sight. The weapon ships with a basic 1-8x variable optic, but most operators replace it with their preferred precision optic within days. The rifle's compact dimensions allow it to be deployed from vehicle windows, building interiors, and rooftop positions where full-length DMRs are unwieldy.

At Φ6,800, the Scalpel occupies the mid-range of the DMR market. It sacrifices the extreme-range capability of longer-barreled platforms for the versatility of a weapon that functions as both a precision rifle and a fighting carbine. For urban operators who need precision capability without dedicating a team member to a full-size DMR, the MPC-9 provides a compelling compromise.
specifications: caliber: 6.5mm caseless effective_range: 600m rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic magazine_capacity: 20 rounds weight: 3.6 kg
tactical_use: The Scalpel provides urban-optimized precision fire. Its compact dimensions allow deployment in confined spaces where full-length DMRs cannot maneuver, while the BCI ballistic computer maintains accuracy despite the short barrel. The weapon's dual role as precision rifle and fighting carbine allows the designated marksman to participate in close-quarters actions without transitioning to a secondary weapon. In urban operations where engagement distances rarely exceed 400 meters, the Scalpel provides all the precision capability needed in a more versatile package.
cultural_context: The Scalpel represents the urbanization of precision marksmanship. Traditional marksmen view it as a compromise that sacrifices range for convenience. Urban operators view it as the evolution of the DMR for the environments where most people actually fight. The debate mirrors the broader tension between frontier and urban combat doctrine that runs through GLMZ's military culture.
story_hooks: A Scalpel operator made a critical shot through two panes of vehicle glass at 400 meters using the BCI ballistic computer's glass-penetration calculation. The shot was technically impossible with a conventional rifle of the same barrel length.
Meridian's compact precision technology has been stolen by a competitor. The knock-off 'Scalpel-type' rifles flooding the market use inferior barrel steel that fails after 2,000 rounds.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, modernist precision carbine with an almost surgical aesthetic. The MPC-9 Scalpel presents a minimalist silhouette—no unnecessary protrusions, no tactical mall-ninja ornamentation. The compact 400mm barrel gives it a balanced, almost pistol-like front end despite its rifle length. The profile suggests engineered efficiency rather than aggressive styling.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 825mm (stock extended), 675mm (stock collapsed). Barrel length: 400mm. Height over rail: 95mm. Width: 65mm at receiver.
physical_description.weight_description: Notably light for a precision platform at 3.6kg—it handles with the nimbleness of a carbine but feels purposeful and solid. Balanced slightly forward of the receiver, encouraging one-handed weapon manipulation in confined spaces.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum receiver with carbon-composite furniture. Barrel is hard-chromed steel with fluted exterior for thermal management.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal gray with brushed titanium accents around the optics rail and magazine well. The receiver displays a subtle satin finish that resists glare. Components show precision machining marks—visible tool marks that read as intentional rather than sloppy.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with brushed titanium and gunmetal accents. Minimal color variation; the weapon reads as a grayscale object.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized pistol grip with subtle micro-texturing for secure purchase even in wet conditions. Fore-end features aggressive stippling that bites into gloved fingers.
distinctive_features: Integrated BCI interface plate behind the optics rail—subtle, flush-mounted, barely visible unless you know to look for it
Fluted barrel visible in the handguard cutouts, dissipating heat along its length
Open-architecture optics rail with tool-less quick-detach points machined into the receiver
Compact muzzle brake with three asymmetrical ports—optimized for recoil management without excessive blast
Recessed magazine well with beveled edges for one-handed mag changes
No dust cover—the design philosophy rejects unnecessary moving parts
Minimalist charging handle integrated flush with the upper receiver
Ambidextrous fire selector controls—subtle levers rather than extended switches
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Meridian Munitions logo (angular M in a circle) etched into the left side of the receiver. 'MPC-9 SCALPEL' stenciled in small, clean serif font directly below. Serial plate mounted on the right side of the lower receiver with raised alphanumerics. Caliber and ballistic computer firmware version printed on the dust cover of the magazine well.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. Light scratches on the aluminum from urban operations—tool marks and scuffs from tactical entries rather than battle damage. Optics rail shows micro-wear from repeated scope mounting/unmounting. The weapon suggests professional use by operators who clean and maintain their equipment scrupulously.
